OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        title:
          title: Title
          description: >-
            The optional honorific title of the pet owner (typically MR, MRS,
            MS or DR). When supplied it is combined with the last name to derive
            the owner's 'salutation'.
          type: string
          maxLength: 10
          example: DR
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. Accepted for backward
            compatibility with the flat address form. On create it is
            normalized and, when the structured 'addressLine1' is supplied,
            the returned value is composed from the structured fields instead.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: >-
            The first line of the pet owner's structured postal address. When a
            non-blank value is supplied the structured form is preferred over the
            flat 'address'. Normalized on create (trimmed, whitespace collapsed,
            upper-cased, common street-type abbreviations expanded).
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: >-
            The optional second line of the pet owner's structured postal
            address. Normalized like 'addressLine1'; when present it is appended
            to the composed 'address' after a single space.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Apartment 4B'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; a leading '+'
            and country code are kept when present, otherwise country code '+61'
            is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the national
            digits. The result must have 8 to 15 digits after the '+'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be
            a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The 4-digit postal code of the pet owner. Optional; when present it
            must be valid for the owner's city per a fixed region table
            (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099). A city with no known
            region accepts any 4-digit postcode. Stored and returned when given.
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered. Optional on create; when not
            supplied it defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO
            'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The pet owner's date of birth. Optional; when supplied it is used to
            derive the owner's 'ageBand'. Given and returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD'
            format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, permits creating this owner even though another owner
            already shares its household (same last name and postcode) that
            would otherwise be rejected as a household duplicate; such a declared
            member is not flagged as a possible duplicate. Write-only; used only
            during create and not persisted or returned.
          type: boolean
          example: true
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as "LastName, FirstName".
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'Franklin, George'
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: >-
                The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName,
                dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'G.F.'
            salutation:
              title: Salutation
              description: >-
                The owner's salutation, derived on read as the title followed by
                a space and the last name (e.g. 'DR who'), or just the last name
                when no title is given.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'DR Franklin'
            telephoneDisplay:
              title: Telephone display
              description: >-
                The stored E.164 'telephone' formatted for humans: the '+' and
                country code, a space, then the national digits grouped in
                threes (e.g. '+61 412 345 678'). Derived on read; the raw
                'telephone' stays in E.164 form.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: '+61 412 345 678'
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                A generated customer code formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where LAST3
                is the upper-cased first three letters of lastName and NNNN is a
                global 4-digit zero-padded sequence assigned on create.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'SMI-0007'
            checkDigit:
              title: Check digit
              description: >-
                A single Luhn check digit (0-9) computed over the digits of the
                customerCode.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9
              readOnly: true
              example: 4
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                A generated membership number formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>'
                where YY is the last two digits of the registrationDate year.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'SMI-0007-M26'
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable shared identifier for owners in the same household,
                assigned deterministically on create as the first 12 hex
                characters of SHA-256 over the normalized last name and postcode.
                Owners with the same last name and postcode automatically share
                the same value.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'A1B2C3D4E5F6'
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: >-
                The derived key used for duplicate detection, formed as
                'normalizedTelephone|<email or empty>|<householdId or empty>'.
                A create is rejected with 409 only when a new owner's whole
                identityKey equals an existing owner's.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: '+61412345678||A1B2C3D4E5F6'
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of existing owners that, at the time this owner was
                created, already shared the same first name and last name
                (compared case-insensitively). Assigned on create.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              readOnly: true
              example: 1
            membershipPoints:
              title: Membership points
              description: >-
                The owner's membership points. The score starts at 0 and gains 2
                when an email is present, 1 when namesakeCount is 0, 2 when the
                household has 3 or more members, and 3 when tenure exceeds 365 days.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              readOnly: true
              example: 3
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-
                The owner's numeric membership level, derived from membershipPoints:
                level 1 for 0-1 points, level 2 for 2-3 points, level 3 for 4-5
                points, and level 4 for 6 or more points.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 4
              readOnly: true
              example: 2
            bulkSignupWarning:
              title: Bulk signup warning
              description: >-
                True when, at the time this owner was created, more than 80 owners

              type: boolean
              readOnly: true
              example: false
            possibleDuplicate:
              title: Possible duplicate
              description: >-
                True when, at the time this owner was created, it was not a hard
                duplicate but shared an existing owner's last name and postcode

              type: boolean
              readOnly: true
              example: false
            possibleDuplicateOf:

            locality:

            pets:

          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'

          description: >-

## Owner deletion is now a soft-delete

**What changed**

1. **`Owner` entity** (`model/Owner.java`) — added a `deleted` field (`@Column(name = "deleted", nullable = false)`, primitive `boolean` defaulting to `false`) with `isDeleted()` / `setDeleted()`. A new owner is `false` by default.

2. **API schema** (`resources/openapi.yml`) — added a read-only `deleted` boolean property to the `Owner` schema. The generated `OwnerDto` picks it up and MapStruct maps it by name, so `GET /api/owners/{id}` now returns `deleted`.

3. **DB schema** (`db/{hsqldb,h2,mysql,postgres}/schema.sql`) — added a `deleted` column (`NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE`) to the `owners` table, so existing seed rows read back as `false`.

4. **Controller** (`rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`):
   - `deleteOwner` now sets `deleted = true` and saves (retaining the row), still returning `204` (2xx), instead of removing the record.
   - The create endpoint's two blocking checks — the hard **identity-key** duplicate loop and the **household** duplicate check (`householdMembers`) — now skip owners flagged `deleted`, so a normally-blocking duplicate is allowed when the only matching owner has been soft-deleted.

**Verification** — both new acceptance tests pass (`coreSoftDeleteFlagsAndRetains`: delete flags `deleted` true while GET still returns the owner; `coreDeletedOwnerIgnoredByDuplicateCheck`: recreating a deep copy of a soft-deleted owner is allowed): `Tests run: 2, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` — `BUILD SUCCESS`.

One thing worth flagging: I left the soft-deleted owner still visible to `GET`/`listOwners` and still counted by the *non-blocking* derivations (`namesakeCount`, `cityOwnerCount`, `customerCode` collision, `possibleDuplicateOf`). The spec only required deleted owners to be readable-with-`deleted=true` and ignored by the **duplicate/identity** checks, so I scoped the exclusion to exactly those checks. If you'd also want deleted owners hidden from list results or excluded from those quota/derivation counts, that's a straightforward follow-up.
